business_problem: Wolt needed a merchant platform that could support large chains with huge catalogs and frequent menu changes without relying on overnight manual updates or a disruptive rewrite of the existing delivery platform.
solution_summary: Wolt built a new merchant and chain-restaurant system on MongoDB Atlas, running it in parallel with its existing AWS platform so it could serve bigger catalogs without interrupting delivery operations. Atlas stores the merchant, menu, and catalog data behind self-service tools that let partners import menus or product lists rather than relying on Wolt staff to make manual updates after hours. The new design gives the team a flexible document model for constantly changing merchant data while keeping rollout risk low because migration happens gradually instead of through a full cutover. Atlas is also integrated with Terraform so Wolt manages infrastructure as code, and engineers use Atlas data directly to analyze their own service-level objectives without first standing up a separate warehouse. The result is a platform that can propagate updates quickly, onboard larger merchants more easily, and continue evolving without the limits of the original architecture.

solution_components.name: MongoDB Atlas
solution_components.role: Stores merchant, menu, and catalog data for Wolt's new merchant platform and supports rapid updates and operational analysis.

data_flow: Merchants import menus and product lists into Wolt's AWS-based merchant platform, MongoDB Atlas stores and updates the catalog data, and those changes are propagated to merchant tools and the consumer delivery experience in near real time.
business_outcome: MongoDB helped Wolt deliver 2-second catalog updates, onboard large merchants faster, and extend its delivery platform without a risky full re-architecture.
